subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students
title: The Motor Load That Drew More Current Than the kW Suggested
featured_title: THE MOTOR LOAD THAT DREW MORE CURRENT THAN THE kW SUGGESTED

presentation.challenge: The load was only 30 kW, but the feeder current was much higher than the kW-only calculation predicted.

practice.primary_question: Why does a three-phase load draw more current when its power factor is below unity?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using P = √3VI for a non-unity-power-factor load and forgetting the power-factor term.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 30 kW three-phase load draws the same current regardless of power factor because real power is unchanged.
case_dna.why_plausible: Students often memorize P = √3VI and omit power factor when the problem gives kW directly.
case_dna.corrected_model: For a balanced three-phase load, P = √3 V_L I_L pf. Lower power factor requires more line current for the same kW and voltage.

problem_statement: A balanced 480 V three-phase motor load consumes 30 kW at 0.75 power factor. A feeder review estimates current as 30,000/(√3×480) = 36.1 A. In operation, current is about 48 A. Diagnose the missing term, calculate the actual line current, and determine the current after correcting power factor to 0.95.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The kW looked safe. The feeder current did not.
gates.prompt: What term is missing from the kW-only current estimate?

gates.label: Theory
gates.heading: Choose the correct three-phase power model

options.label: Use P = √3 V_L I_L pf, so lower power factor increases current for the same kW
options.reason: Real power includes the power-factor term.

options.label: Use P = √3 V_L I_L for every balanced load
options.reason: That form assumes unity power factor.

options.label: Multiply the kW-only current by power factor
options.reason: Solving for current divides by power factor.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the line current
gates.prompt: For 30 kW, 480 V three phase, and pf = 0.75, what line current (A) do you expect?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Read the feeder current
gates.result: The line current is about 48.1 A.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the current
gates.prompt: Use I = P/(√3 V_L pf) with P = 30,000 W, V_L = 480 V, and pf = 0.75.
gates.success: I ≈ 48.1 A. The 36.1 A estimate omitted power factor.
gates.hint: Power factor belongs in the denominator.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The power triangle explains the extra current

cards.text: The load consumes 30 kW at 0.75 power factor.
Apparent power is S = P/pf = 40 kVA.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the feeder calculation
report: C1. The load is 30 kW at 480 V three phase.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: The calculation assumes unity power factor.

evidence_choices.label: I = 30,000/(√3×480×0.75) ≈ 48.1 A
evidence_choices.reason: This includes the missing power-factor term.

correction.template: Including pf = 0.75, the line current is about {current} A.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Raise power factor to 0.95
gates.constraint: Keep 30 kW real power and 480 V line voltage.

options.label: Current remains 48.1 A
options.reason: Improved power factor reduces apparent power and line current.

options.label: Current becomes 36.1 A exactly
options.reason: 36.1 A corresponds to unity power factor.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the power-factor rule
gates.prompt: For fixed three-phase kW and voltage, what happens to line current when power factor improves?
gates.explanation: Improving power factor reduces current for the same real power and line voltage.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the power-factor correction
gates.confirmation: I confirm that three-phase real-power calculations must include power factor when the load is not unity power factor.

items.label: What was assumed
items.value: The load was treated as unity power factor.

seo.seo_title: Three-Phase Power Factor Current: Why 30 kW Draws 48 A | FE E-029
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Case E-029: a 30 kW, 480 V three-phase load at 0.75 power factor draws about 48 A. Diagnose the missing pf term and correct it.
seo.focus_keyphrase: three phase power factor current FE exam
seo.excerpt: A kW-only three-phase current calculation can look correct and still undersize a feeder when power factor is below unity.
seo.direct_answer: For a balanced three-phase load, P = √3 V_L I_L pf. At 30 kW, 480 V, and pf = 0.75, the line current is about 48.1 A. Omitting power factor gives only 36.1 A.

faqs.q: How do you calculate three-phase current from kW and power factor?
Does improving power factor reduce current?
faqs.a: Yes. For fixed real power and line voltage, higher power factor reduces line current.
